name: flint
why: A serious C library for number theory that lets you play with real algebraic computation at home.

brief.what_it_is: FLINT (Fast Library for Number Theory) is a C library for number theory, released under the GNU LGPL version 3 or later. It provides arithmetic in the integers, rationals, algebraic, real, complex and p-adic numbers, finite fields and number fields, plus univariate and multivariate polynomials, power series and matrices. Its functions include primality testing, integer factorisation, multivariate polynomial GCD and factorisation, FFTs, special functions, exact and approximate linear algebra and LLL. Input is C calls on library types; output is the computed numbers, polynomials, matrices and so on.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents FLINT as a fast, mature number theory library for all operand sizes, from single-word to multi-gigabyte, which many computer algebra systems use as a back end. It also says its developers have published more than 20 papers describing new algorithms first implemented in or on top of FLINT.
brief.how_it_works: The page says FLINT picks automatically between basecase, intermediate, asymptotically fast and special-purpose algorithms depending on the size and structure of the problem. Many algorithms are multithreaded and some key functions use SIMD acceleration. Real and complex numbers use ball arithmetic, which gives arbitrary precision with rigorous error bounds.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install steps, build commands or package names. It says FLINT runs on Linux, macOS and Windows on typical hardware, and that bindings exist for Python, Julia, Haskell and C++. The Downloads and Documentation sections are linked from the navigation, but I did not follow them, so build and install details are unverified.
brief.standout: FLINT is a serious C library, not a toy or classroom tool: it is the back end under SageMath, OSCAR, Singular, Macaulay2, Maple and Mathematica. Version 3.0 merged the previously separate Arb, Antic and Calcium libraries, so one codebase now covers exact and rigorous real and complex arithmetic.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage says 'Last updated: 2026-06-29', it advertises a FLINT workshop in Bordeaux for 15–19 June 2026, and it describes the FLINT 3.0 release. I did not check a release date or commit history.
brief.caveats: The page gives no install instructions, and the Downloads and Documentation pages were not read. Working with C and its API assumes a systems-programming background. The scout note's 'play with real algebraic computation at home' is the scout's wording, not the project's; the project describes itself as a developer-facing library. The page does not say whether the bindings are complete or maintained to the same standard as the C library.
quotes: FLINT is a C library for doing number theory, freely available under the GNU Lesser General Public License version 3 or later.
FLINT is designed for all operand sizes, from single-word to multi-gigabyte.
FLINT is the work of dozens of contributors, spanning 15+ years of development.
